C1:
Problem 1: Humanoid:MoveTo times out after 8 seconds. If the zombie hasn't reached the goal by then, it stops and MoveToFinished fires with reached=false. Your code ignores that boolean, so it prints "arrived" anyway. Fix: check `local reached = hum.MoveToFinished:Wait()`, or move in short legs and call MoveTo again before 8 s.
Problem 2: MoveTo walks in a straight line and does no pathfinding, so walls block it. Fix: use PathfindingService.
```lua
local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({AgentRadius=2, AgentHeight=5, AgentCanJump=true})
local ok = pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, root.Position, target.Position)
if ok and path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success then
  for _, wp in path:GetWaypoints() do
    if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then hum.Jump = true end
    hum:MoveTo(wp.Position)
    if not hum.MoveToFinished:Wait() then break end -- stuck, so recompute
  end
end
```
Other points: recompute when path.Blocked fires or the target moves, and throttle repaths to every 0.5-1 s. Call `root:SetNetworkOwner(nil)` so the server owns the NPC's physics and it doesn't stutter.
C2:
ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn defaults to true. Each respawn destroys the PlayerGui copy of the ScreenGui and clones it fresh from StarterGui. The LocalScript inside restarts too, so its local variables reset to the defaults.
Fix: set ResetOnSpawn = false on the ScreenGui. The GUI and its script then survive respawns. Alternatively, keep settings in a place that outlives the GUI: a ModuleScript or a LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts, or attributes on the Player. Settings meant to persist across sessions (music off) should go to the server and be saved in a DataStore, then reapplied on join. Don't let GUI code depend on the character without handling CharacterAdded.
C3:
Animation replication rule: animations played on a client replicate only for characters or models whose Animator that client owns. In practice that means the local player's own character, whose Animator was created by the server or by Roblox. So your sword swing replicates.
The shopkeeper NPC is owned by the server. Animations a client plays on it stay local, so only that player sees the wave.
An Animator created by Instance.new in a LocalScript exists only on that client. The server and other players never see the Animator, so nothing replicates.
Fix: play NPC animations from a server Script, using the Animator that exists on the server (`hum:FindFirstChildOfClass("Animator")` or one the server creates) with Animator:LoadAnimation(anim):Play(). That replicates to everyone. For purely cosmetic NPC idles you can instead have every client play the animation locally. Don't create Animators on the client for your own character either. Use the existing one under Humanoid.
C4:
(1) A Sound parented to Workspace or a service (not a Part or Attachment) is non-positional: it plays globally at full volume for everyone. Fix: parent it to the barrel Part or an Attachment so it is 3D and attenuates with distance. Set RollOffMode and RollOffMinDistance/RollOffMaxDistance.
(2) Positional sounds fade according to RollOffMode, RollOffMinDistance and RollOffMaxDistance. Inverse rolloff, the default, drops quickly. Fix: raise RollOffMinDistance (the full-volume radius) and RollOffMaxDistance (for example 300-500). Use Linear or InverseTapered so it stays audible further out. Volume alone won't carry it.
(3) Loaded fires only once, when loading finishes. If the sound is already loaded when Wait() is called, the event never fires again, so the script hangs. Fix: `if not siren.IsLoaded then siren.Loaded:Wait() end` (optionally with a timeout), or preload with ContentProvider:PreloadAsync. Also check that the SoundId is valid and that the place has permission to use the asset.
C5:
Cause 1: the second argument to Raycast is a direction vector whose length is the ray distance. A .Unit vector is only 1 stud long, so the ray almost never hits anything and returns nil. Indexing nil.Instance then errors.
Cause 2: the ray starts inside your own head and character, so it hits your own parts.
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {player.Character}
local origin = head.Position
local dir = (mouseHit - origin).Unit * 500  -- max range
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if result then
  print(result.Instance.Name, result.Position)
end
```
Always nil-check the result. For a real gun, send the aim direction to the server and redo or validate the raycast there. Never trust the client to report hits.
C6:
Only one tween can control a given property of an instance at a time. When a new tween on BackgroundTransparency starts, the hover tween still running on that property is cancelled. It stays wherever it stopped (Completed fires with Cancelled), and nothing restores it. When the flash ends it goes to its own fixed value, not to the current hover state. So the hover and flash tweens fight and leave inconsistent end states.
Structure it as a small state machine:
- Track the state (hovered: bool, pressed: bool).
- Write one function that computes the target value from that state and plays the tween, and keep a reference to the current tween. Cancel it before starting a new one.
- MouseEnter/MouseLeave set hovered and call the function. Click plays the flash and, when it completes, tweens back to the target for the current state, not to a hardcoded value.
- Or animate different properties so they don't conflict: hover on BackgroundTransparency, click on UIScale.Scale or a separate overlay Frame.
Also debounce clicks, and do purchase logic on the server, not in the animation.

C10:
```lua
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("Gems")
local function addGems(player, amount)
  assert(typeof(amount) == "number" and amount == amount and amount > 0 and amount % 1 == 0)
  local key = "Player_" .. player.UserId
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    local ok, newValue = pcall(function()
      return store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
        old = tonumber(old) or 0
        return old + amount
      end)
    end)
    if ok then return true, newValue end
    warn("UpdateAsync failed:", newValue)
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  return false
end
```
Callback rules:
- Treat the old value as possibly nil (new player) and return the new value.
- Return nil to cancel the write without changing anything.
- Keep the callback pure and fast: no yields, no side effects, and no task.wait or other async calls inside. Roblox may call it more than once if another server writes in between.
Error handling:
- Run on the server only.
- Wrap the call in pcall and retry with backoff, within DataStore request budgets.
- Never assume success. Report failure so the caller can roll back or retry.
- Validate the amount on the server.
- For whole-profile games, prefer session-cached data saved periodically and on PlayerRemoving/BindToClose over one write per change.

C13:
Use MemoryStoreService (a MemoryStoreQueue or MemoryStoreSortedMap keyed by skill), not DataStore. DataStores are slow, durable, have tight write limits and per-key write cooldowns, and offer no queue semantics.
Limits:
- Memory: 64 KB + 1.2 KB per user across the experience.
- Requests: 1,000 + 120 x CCU per minute.
- Each queue or map is one partition, roughly 30k units/min.
- Max item 32 KB.
- Max expiration 45 days (3,888,000 s).
- Queue ReadAsync items are invisible for 30 s by default, then reappear unless RemoveAsync is called.
- Data is not durable.
Design:
- Short TTLs on tickets (about 2 min, refreshed while waiting).
- One ticket per party.
- A single matchmaker leader elected through a HashMap/SortedMap lease (renewed every few seconds).
- Read a batch, form matches by skill, then remove matched items. Re-add leftovers before removing.
- Make the steps after a read idempotent, since reads are at-least-once.
- Widen the skill window over wait time.
- Use MessagingService to notify lobbies, and TeleportService with ShouldReserveServer to send each match.
- pcall and back off on throttling errors.
C14:
Flow:
1. A lobby server Script collects the 4 players and validates the party.
2. Save and release each player's data: flush the DataStore and end the session lock.
3. Teleport with `TeleportService:TeleportAsync(matchPlaceId, players, options)`, where TeleportOptions.ShouldReserveServer = true. Alternatively, call ReserveServer once and set ReservedServerAccessCode.
4. In the match server, load each player's coins and loadout from the DataStore, the source of truth. Optionally write a server-side ticket (MemoryStore or DataStore, keyed by match id with a member list) and pass only its id through options:SetTeleportData().
Pitfalls:
- Teleport data travels through the client and can be spoofed (GetJoinData is only partly trusted). Never pass coins or anything valuable through it, and read it on the server via player:GetJoinData().
- TeleportAsync must run on the server, wrapped in pcall. Handle TeleportInitFailed with a few retries and a fallback.
- Don't combine ShouldReserveServer, ReservedServerAccessCode and ServerInstanceId.
- Never send reserved access codes to clients.
- Both places must be in the same experience.
- Teleports don't work in Studio.
- Avoid save/load races by saving before you teleport, or with session locking.
C15:
Never trust the client for prices or outcomes. The client should only send intent: `BuyItem:FireServer("Sword")`, or better an item id.
Server responsibilities:
- Look up the price in a server-side catalog (a ServerStorage/ServerScriptService module).
- Validate the argument types and that the item exists and is for sale.
- Check that the player can buy it (level, already owned).
- Check the server-held balance, subtract and grant atomically in server data, then save.
- Rate-limit or debounce per player so double fires can't double-buy.
- Return the result with a RemoteFunction or a reply event.
Client responsibilities: display only. It shows prices from a replicated read-only copy of the catalog and shows the result, but it decides nothing.
Also:
- Keep currency only in server data, never in client values.
- Leaderstats are display.
- Log suspicious requests.
- Robux purchases go through MarketplaceService and ProcessReceipt, never a RemoteEvent.

Use Roblox localization (LocalizationTable and LocalizationService) with automatic translation for static UI. For runtime text, don't concatenate strings. Use keyed entries with parameters, for example key "QuestProgress" with source "You collected {count} of {total} {item}" and es/pt/de translations in the table (via the Cloud Localization Table, CSV upload or the translator portal).
In code, get a Translator with `LocalizationService:GetTranslatorForPlayerAsync(player)` (pcall it, and fall back to GetTranslatorForPlayer). Format with `translator:FormatByKey("QuestProgress", {count = 12, total = 20, item = ...})`, then set the label's text. When you set text you translated yourself, turn AutoLocalize off on that label so it isn't translated twice.
Translators can reorder parameters, which handles grammar differences. Handle plurals with separate keys.
NPC names:
- Put them in their own TextLabels with AutoLocalize = false.
- Pass them as parameters, or exclude them from capture or the table.
- Make sure the automatic text capture doesn't pick up names or player-generated text.
Format numbers and dates per locale. Leave room for German text, which is longer: use TextScaled or AutomaticSize.
C17:
Yes, for the high-frequency, cosmetic part. Steering and throttle snapshots sent 20 times per second, and exhaust effects, can be lost without harm, because the next update replaces the last. UnreliableRemoteEvent avoids the reliable channel's resend and ordering delays, which cause latency spikes and queue buildup.
Rules:
- Each payload must be 1,000 bytes or less. Larger ones are dropped silently.
- No delivery guarantee and no ordering. Add a sequence number or timestamp and ignore stale packets, using wrap-aware comparison.
- Send compact state (numbers or small buffers), not instances or big tables.
- Validate on the server: finite numbers, clamped ranges, rate limits.
- Keep authoritative car physics and position through network ownership and replication. The remote is only for extra inputs and visuals.
Lap completions, finish order, rewards and any start/stop state must use a reliable RemoteEvent, and the server should validate them through checkpoints. A lost "stop" event would leave an effect running forever.
C18:
Unanchored parts near a player get automatic network ownership. The server hands the boss's physics simulation to the nearest player's client. Ownership switching back and forth as players approach causes the stutter. While a client owns the boss, that client simulates it. An exploiter can then move it freely and fire Touched locally, faking or avoiding damage.
Fix:
- Call `bossRootPart:SetNetworkOwner(nil)` on the server for the boss's assemblies after spawning. Do it after the boss is parented, and again if the assembly is rebuilt. This keeps physics on the server and stops ownership changes. Check with GetNetworkOwner and CanSetNetworkOwnership.
- Do damage on the server and validate it: server-side spatial queries (GetPartsInPart, Raycast or magnitude checks against hitboxes) on attack frames with cooldowns, rather than trusting Touched that clients can influence.
- Never accept "I got hit" or "I hit the boss" reports from the client without checking distance and timing.
- Don't anchor and CFrame the boss if you need Humanoid physics. Server ownership is enough.
C19:
Structure:
- Put each turret, or a group of turrets (for example 60 turrets split over 6-12 Actors), under its own Actor with a script inside. Scripts within the same Actor run sequentially, so you need several Actors.
- In each Actor, connect with `RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel(fn)`, or call `task.desynchronize()`.
- In the parallel phase, read positions and do `workspace:Raycast` for line of sight. Spatial queries and property reads are safe there.
- Store the results, then call `task.synchronize()` before writing anything: changing properties, firing remotes, applying damage or creating instances.
- Alternatively, use one script that sends batches to worker Actors with actor:SendMessage and BindToMessageParallel.
Restrictions:
- In the parallel phase you can't create, parent or destroy instances or set most properties. Unsafe API calls error.
- No `require` in parallel.
- Each Actor has its own Luau VM, so module state isn't shared. Messages are copied and can't contain functions.
- Share data through SharedTable, using SharedTable.increment/update for atomic updates (update callbacks may rerun).
- Don't desynchronize and synchronize several times per frame per turret.
- Use the MicroProfiler to check that work actually spreads across threads.
Also reduce work: skip line-of-sight checks for out-of-range targets and stagger checks over several frames.
C20:
Teleport: before moving the character, call `player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(destination, timeout)` from the server, wrapped in pcall. After it yields, check that the player and character still exist, then PivotTo. The request is temporary and not guaranteed, so also give arrival a short grace period: anchor the root or briefly hold the player at a spawn platform until the floor has streamed in.
Settings:
- Make the dungeon entrance and other critical models Atomic or Persistent through Model.ModelStreamingMode. Atomic loads the whole model at once. Persistent always stays loaded, so use it sparingly. PersistentPerPlayer works with AddPersistentPlayer.
- StreamingMinRadius (default 64) is the area always loaded around the player. Keep it modest.
- StreamingTargetRadius (default 1024) is how far content streams in. Lower it to cut memory on phones.
- StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic removes content beyond the target radius proactively. LowMemory, the default, streams out only under memory pressure.
- StreamingIntegrityMode (for example PauseOutsideLoadedArea) stops players moving into unloaded space.
- Use LOD (ModelLevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh) for distant models.
Client scripts must use WaitForChild or CollectionService signals, because instances appear and disappear. Never assume parts exist.
C21:
Structure: InputContext > InputAction > InputBinding, all instances.
- InputContext is a group you enable or disable, with Priority and Sink.
- InputAction has a Type: Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D or ViewportPosition. Its events are Pressed, Released and StateChanged, and it has GetState() and Fire().
- InputBinding has KeyCode, composite directional keys, UIButton for touch, modifiers, PressedThreshold, Scale and ResponseCurve. Give each action keyboard, gamepad and touch bindings.

```lua
action.StateChanged:Connect(function(isDown)
  humanoid.WalkSpeed = isDown and 24 or 16
  SprintRemote:FireServer(isDown) -- server validates
end)
```
For a held state you can also poll `action:GetState()`.

It breaks `require(PlayerModule):GetControls()` hacks, code that relies on old input sinking, and forked player scripts. Forks need CreateDefaultPlayerModule handled.

Change: age checks became mandatory for chat. A user verifies through facial age estimation, ID or parental controls and is placed in an age group: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20 or 21+.
